summary.title: How to get lucky?
summary.one_liner: Learn James H. Austin's four types of chance (blind, active, discerned, personality luck) and how to prepare for each through consuming, producing, and engaging.
keywords: derek sivers breakthroughs come from people
takeaways: Austin classifies luck into four types: blind luck, active luck (motion), discerned luck (recognizing faint clues), and personality luck (from distinctive behavior).
Active luck comes from doing things that interest you without a clear goal, since stumbling on opportunities requires moving.
Discerned luck depends on a prepared mind that spots trends and significance others miss.
Preparation follows a Consume, Produce, Engage loop: learn widely, favor action and output over perfection, and share work to connect with people.
Luck and hard work both shape outcomes, and the author argues you can deliberately become luckier.
summary.summary: A personal essay by a CTO who argues that much of his career success came from luck as well as hard work. He structures the piece around James H. Austin's four types of chance, giving a concrete example from his own career for each. He closes with a practical self-guided routine of consuming ideas, producing content, and engaging with people to prepare for luck.
